name: Ketovore

lead: Ketovore is very low-carb eating centred on meat and animal fat, with a small selection of plant foods allowed. People follow it to drop body fat and the puffy, bloated look, with a plate that is easy to plan.

The chain is lower carbohydrate intake, which pushes the liver to make ketone bodies as an alternative fuel, and followers report reduced appetite and less water retention, so the face and midsection look leaner. The name is informal and no trials have tested ketovore itself; the research comes from ketogenic and low-carb diet studies.

paras: Most people build meals around beef, eggs, fish and animal fats, then add a few low-carb vegetables or other plants for variety and fibre. It is usually followed as an everyday eating style rather than a short cleanse, and followers commonly report early scale changes within the first weeks as water and appetite shift.

Ketogenic diets can cause constipation, raised blood lipids and kidney stones, and clinical use is medically supervised. Dietetic bodies describe the neighbouring carnivore diet as a fad diet and cite low fibre and higher LDL cholesterol. People with kidney, liver or lipid conditions, or who are pregnant, should check with a clinician first.

angle.text: Ketovore is used for keto-style fat loss with a simple meat-centred plate, aiming for a leaner body and less bloat. Cutting carbs lowers appetite and water retention, which shows up as a slimmer, less puffy look. Research comes from keto and low-carb diets generally, as the hybrid has no trials of its own.

lead: Ketovore is an informal label for a ketogenic, very low-carbohydrate diet that centers on meat and other animal foods while allowing some low-carbohydrate plant foods. It sits between a standard ketogenic diet and the carnivore diet, which allows only animal products [1]. People adopt it to get leaner, which makes muscle definition and the jawline and face look sharper, and some report clearer skin and steadier energy for training.

The ketogenic diet is a high-fat, adequate-protein, low-carbohydrate diet used in conventional medicine mainly for drug-resistant epilepsy. The carnivore diet gained social-media attention from 2018, when former orthopaedic surgeon Shawn Baker promoted it, and Jordan Peterson and his daughter Mikhaila became prominent followers [1]. Ketovore is described by its followers as a less restrictive version of that approach.
Dietetic bodies such as the British Dietetic Association classify the carnivore diet as a fad diet [1]. No clinical trial of a diet specifically called ketovore has been published.

paras: The term is used informally rather than defined by a medical body. It generally denotes a keto diet in which animal foods dominate and a limited set of low-carbohydrate plants is included. A related variant, the animal-based diet, adds fruit, honey and raw dairy to carnivore eating [1].
On T Nation, one member described adopting a food list as "basically Ketovore" for a body-composition phase, cooking in bulk to control calories [2].

Wikipedia reports that low-carbohydrate diets can produce somewhat more weight loss than low-fat diets in the short and medium term, that the advantage fades over time, and that a 2022 Cochrane review found no benefit at two years compared with balanced diets [3]. When calorie intake is held constant, body-fat change does not appear to differ much with large shifts in fat versus carbohydrate, according to the Endocrine Society as summarized there [3].

A 2025 cross-sectional study of 21 adults who reached type 2 diabetes remission through diet and exercise recorded that 14% followed a "ketovore/carnivore" diet and 52% a low or very low carbohydrate diet; it examined glucose profiles and did not test ketovore for appearance [4].

Wikipedia reports that carnivore eating excludes fruit and vegetables, is low in fiber, can raise LDL cholesterol, and has been called potentially dangerous by dietitians and physicians [1]. In clinical use of ketogenic diets, reported adverse effects include constipation, raised blood lipids and kidney stones, and the diet is started under medical supervision. Low-carbohydrate diets are also associated with constipation, headache, bad breath and cramps in a summarized meta-analysis, and long-term use with higher LDL cholesterol [3].

On T Nation, a lifter reported that however much they tried carnivore, keto, ketovore or low carb, adding carbohydrates and calories back improved recovery and how they felt [5]. This sits alongside other members who use the pattern for cutting phases [2].
No studies found on a diet specifically called ketovore. Related studies cover ketogenic and low-carbohydrate diets generally [3].
